nodes.label: Lead triage rubric and answer key
nodes.rationale: Every label in data/leads.jsonl was written by hand against these rules and no model produced any label. If Claude had written the key, scoring Claude against it would measure self-agreement and Jev would lose a point everywhere Claude was wrong. The rules are published so readers can disagree, and the fix for a mislabelled lead is a pull request against src/build_dataset.py.

nodes.label: Rubric: disqualify rule
nodes.rationale: True for job applicants, students or academics asking for free access, vendors and agencies selling to us, employees of a direct competitor, and generic spam. False for everyone else, including weak and early buyers, short messages and gmail addresses. Competitors are judged by where they work: L009 and L010 read like ordinary demo requests.

nodes.label: Rubric: icp_fit rule
nodes.rationale: True when the company sells to businesses, has 50 or more people, and the role touches revenue, marketing, operations or data or is an executive. Judge the company and not the email domain (L016, a Cisco buyer on gmail), and look at what the role does (L044, a Facilities Coordinator at Salesforce, is no fit).

nodes.label: Judgment independence (icp_fit judged separately from disqualify)
nodes.rationale: A RevOps manager at a competitor is a fit on company and role and still gets rejected, because the routing rule checks disqualification first. Keeping the questions separate stops one judgment from quietly absorbing another, and a model that confuses the two shows up in the numbers.

nodes.label: Rubric: segment rule
nodes.rationale: Straight from headcount: 1000 or more is enterprise, 200 to 999 mid_market, under 200 smb. It is the easiest question and is in the set on purpose as a floor: getting it wrong means the model did not read the record.

nodes.label: Rubric: intent rule
nodes.rationale: Four ordered levels (none, researching, evaluating, ready_to_buy) read from the message itself and never from company quality. Support tickets from large existing customers (L046, L048) are none. An existing customer adding 20 seats (L047) is ready_to_buy, because expansion is a purchase.

nodes.label: Rubric: five-branch routing rule
nodes.rationale: Routing is a rule, so it runs as one. spec.route() takes the four judgments and returns reject, ae_now, sdr_sequence, self_serve or nurture, runs over the answer key and every model's output alike, and no model is ever asked to route. Five branches are free, instant and testable, and a model call there buys nothing and adds a way to fail.

nodes.label: 60-lead label distribution
nodes.rationale: 12 disqualify and 48 not; 44 icp_fit and 16 not; 24 enterprise, 19 mid_market, 17 smb; intent 13 none, 14 researching, 20 evaluating, 13 ready_to_buy; routes 16 ae_now, 19 nurture, 10 sdr_sequence, 12 reject, 3 self_serve. self_serve has only 3 cases, so treat that row as directional.

nodes.label: Deliberately awkward lead set
nodes.rationale: Roughly a third of the leads are awkward on purpose: real buyers on personal email, competitors posing as buyers, huge companies with no fit, senior people with no intent, and two nearly empty messages. A set of obvious cases puts every model at 100% and tells you nothing.
